comment: My laptop and email account weren't ready until my third day, so I spent two days reading PDFs.
My supervisor checked in every day the first week. That made a huge difference.
I filled out my emergency contact and tax information on three different forms.
Nobody told me who to contact about my office keys. I asked four people.
The orientation sessions were six hours long and half of it didn't apply to my job.
I couldn't log in to the HR system for over a week, so I couldn't finish my benefits enrollment.
Having an assigned buddy on my team was the best part of onboarding.
So much paperwork. Some of it asked for the same information I'd already given during hiring.
It took two weeks to get my parking permit, and I got a ticket in the meantime.
My computer arrived without the software I needed for teaching, and the first week of classes had already started.
I never knew who to ask about basic things like printing or ordering supplies.
My manager walked me through our team's projects and introduced me to everyone. Very welcoming.
The paper forms had to be signed, scanned and emailed. Why isn't this online?
Building access didn't work on my first day and I had to wait outside for someone to let me in.
The compliance trainings took most of my first week and felt rushed and generic.
My ID card wasn't printed until week two, so I couldn't use the library or the gym.
My department chair met with me before I started and answered every question. Great experience.
I got conflicting answers from HR and my department about when my benefits start.
Shared drive access wasn't set up, so I couldn't see any of my predecessor's files.
I had to submit my direct deposit form twice because the first one was lost.
There's no single page that lists who handles what. I kept emailing the wrong office.
The training videos were fine, but there were too many of them in one day.
My team lunch on day one helped me feel part of the group right away.
Accounts for the ticketing system and email were all ready on day one. Smooth start.
Too many forms, and several were outdated versions that got rejected.
